Subject: Fincobank — Audit logs & data access (follow-up from discovery call)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on from our discovery:

1) Audit log scope: you mentioned wanting visibility into who accessed what and when for customer data and model requests (per-user access, export events, admin actions).
2) Retention & exports: you asked about configurable retention windows and export formats for regulatory requests (CSV/JSON preferred).
3) PII handling: clarity on fields that may contain PII and options for redaction/masking in exported logs.
4) Residency & access controls: whether logs can be retained in-region and who within your org vs. Redwood can access exports.
5) Evidence for SOC 2 / audit: sample artifacts we can provide (export samples, retention policy, access controls).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send a sample audit-log export (CSV + JSON samples) showing the typical fields we log and masking options.
- Marissa (solutions engineer) will join a 30-min technical follow-up to walk through export formats and retention controls.
- We’ll also share our redacted Data Processing Addendum and the audit logs export spec.

Can you confirm the following so we scope the artefacts correctly before the follow-up?
- Required retention window (years/months) for audit logs?
- Any fields you must retain unmasked for compliance?
- Does Fincobank require logs to be resident in a specific region or cloud tenancy?

Attaching the call recap deck and our audit-logs export spec for quick review.

Subject: Re: Fincobank — Audit logs & data access (follow-up from discovery call)

Hi Dylan —

Appreciate the clear recap — very helpful. A few answers below to help you scope the samples:

- Retention window: our compliance team requires audit logs retained for 7 years for customer-facing access and export events.
- Required fields: we need unmasked identifiers for user_id and admin_id for forensic investigations. IP addresses and timestamps must be preserved. We are comfortable with masking names and email addresses in downstream analytics exports, but not in forensic exports.
- Export formats: CSV is our preferred format for ingestion into our internal SIEM, but JSON with structured fields is also acceptable.
- Residency: logs for Fincobank customers must be stored and exported from US regions only.
- Access controls: only designated security and compliance users at Fincobank should be able to download raw exports; others can see aggregated dashboards.

Also, can you include any notes about how Redwood surfaces who at Redwood has accessed production logs (auditable access list)? We will need that for our infosec review.

If possible, please share a sample CSV (with synthetic data) showing the columns and redaction options before our next call. I’ll coordinate with Tom and Legal to confirm availability for the technical follow-up — likely Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Thanks,

Sarah Li
Director, Information Security | Fincobank
sarah.li@fincobank.com

Subject: Re: Fincobank — Audit logs & data access (follow-up from discovery call)

Thanks Sarah — that’s exactly the level of detail we need. Short answers and next steps below:

- Retention: we can configure per-account retention windows; 7 years is supported. I’ll include the policy snippet and retention-control UI screenshots in the package.
- Required fields: we’ll provide two export flavors:
  * Forensic export (raw): user_id, admin_id, event_type, resource, timestamp, IP, request_id — all unmasked.
  * Analytics export (masked): PII fields (name, email) replaced with hashed IDs; IPs optionally truncated.
- Formats: CSV and JSON both supported; we’ll attach a synthetic CSV sample and a JSON example.
- Residency: we can pin logs to US region (AWS us-east-1) for export and storage. We’ll document the configuration.
- Redwood access: all accesses by Redwood staff to production logs are recorded in our internal access audit log (user, role, timestamp, reason) and we can provide a redacted sample showing access events for audit.

Proposed immediate deliverables (by EOD):
- Sample forensic CSV (synthetic data) and JSON example.
- Short write-up on retention config and residency.
- Redacted sample of Redwood staff access events.
- Data Processing Addendum link and our SOC 2 artifact checklist.

Can you confirm whether Fincobank needs the CSV columns in a specific order or if we should follow our standard export spec (attached)? Also, please share a couple of available time slots for the technical follow-up — Marissa and Aditya are available Wed 1–3pm PST or Thu 10–11am PST.

I’ve attached the sample spec and our retention policy again for reference.

[Attachment: redwood-audit-logs-export-spec.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: redwood-data-retention-policy.pdf (application/pdf)]

Best,

Dylan
